summary: The candidate is a partial, experimental SGLang adapter, not a verified resolution of the original SageAttention request. The recorded base rejects `sage`; the candidate registers it, parses split prefill/decode selection, rejects ROCm, and its gathered-prefix/GQA adapter matches an independent PyTorch SDPA reference on the assigned AMD GPU when the SageAttention callable is replaced. The actual SageAttention package, native INT8 Q/K kernels, CUDA numerical behavior, model quality, and performance claim were not built or executed. In addition, the exact dependency revision named by the candidate dispatches SM80/86/89/90/120 but raises on SM100, while the candidate documentation describes support broadly as NVIDIA CUDA only.

tests.what_was_measured: At the exact recorded base, argparse rejected `--prefill-attention-backend sage`; `sage` was absent from both ATTENTION_BACKEND_CHOICES and ATTENTION_BACKENDS. This reproduces the missing-feature failure. See base-reproduction.txt.

The candidate's 17 tests, 18 subtests, and resolution regression suite passed. Its numerical tests substitute torch.scaled_dot_product_attention for the real SageAttention callable, so they measure adapter behavior rather than quantized native output. See candidate-tests.txt.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-71995f824f5e/venv/bin/python <independent gathered-prefix, GQA, CLI, ROCm, and mask adversarial probe>
tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI355X, split CLI selection and registry wiring passed; ROCm admission failed closed; the inherited dense paged-KV gather for a prefix-5/extend-3 causal GQA case matched an explicit bottom-right causal PyTorch reference; sliding-window/mask input was rejected. The Sage callable was still a reference substitute. See independent-adversarial.txt.

tests.command: git checkout d9704247a5139ab4c03bf7fc6b35cc0e2cbb5ea4 in a private SageAttention source clone; inspect setup.py and sageattention/core.py
tests.what_was_measured: The exact documented dependency revision was inspected. Its public sageattn dispatcher selects SM80, SM86, SM89, SM90, and SM120, and otherwise raises `Unsupported CUDA architecture`; there is no SM100 dispatch branch despite setup.py recognizing SM100. See architecture-evidence.txt.

gpu_evidence: Independent adapter numerics executed on one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. No SageAttention CUDA kernel executed; the installed environment has no `sageattention` module and no NVIDIA GPU.
remaining_counterexamples: On NVIDIA SM100, the exact documented SageAttention revision's public `sageattn` dispatcher raises `ValueError: Unsupported CUDA architecture: sm100`; the candidate neither rejects this configuration during admission nor documents the exclusion.
No real SageAttention import, native build, or INT8 Q/K kernel execution was demonstrated, so installation and runtime behavior on every claimed CUDA architecture remain unverified.
No independent numerical comparison used quantized SageAttention output; replacing `sageattn` with full-precision PyTorch SDPA cannot establish the original same-accuracy claim.

No end-to-end model serving, perplexity/task-quality, long-context, throughput, latency, or memory measurement was performed, so the original approximately 2x inference-speed motivation remains unverified.
The backend's dense paged-KV gather and materialized GQA/MQA expansion may dominate or erase kernel gains, especially outside the recommended prefill-only split; this has not been measured.
remaining_limitations: The assigned architecture is AMD gfx950 under ROCm 7.2; upstream SageAttention is CUDA-only.
No NVIDIA device, CUDA toolkit path, supported model weights, or real SageAttention installation was available.

The candidate changes no SGLang native source, so there was no candidate native component to rebuild. The external native dependency could not be built meaningfully for the assigned ROCm architecture.

The deterministic tiny Llama fixture was not used because a transport smoke on ROCm with a different attention backend cannot validate the CUDA-only quantized kernel, accuracy, or performance contract.
